net.lemnik.eodsql

Annotation Type Call


  • @Target(value=METHOD)
 @Retention(value=RUNTIME)
public @interface Call

    The @Call annotation is used to mark methods within a Query interface that will execute a stored procedure. The @Call annotation contains much the same data as a @Select annotation.

    A method annotated by @Call has the same conditions placed on it as a method annotated by @Select. They may have the same return types, delcare the same Exceptions, etc. Here is an example of how a @Call is used:

    public class User {
        public Integer id;
        public String username;
    }

    public interface UserQuery extends BaseQuery {
        @Call( "call FIND_USER (?1)")
        public DataSet<User> getUserById(int id);
    }

    Columns that cannot be mapped to fields or methods are ignored, as are fields and methods that cannot be mapped to columns. @Call SQL uses the exact same query parser as the Select annotation, and so can also accept complex types as it's parameters, and insert their fields into the SQL query.

    Since:
    2.0
    Author:
    tsmith
    See Also:
    Update, Select

    • Element Detail

      • value

        public abstract String value
        The SQL query to execute on the database. The result set of the query will be mapped to the datatype specified in the method declaration.
        See Also:
        call()
        Default:
        ""

      • call

        public abstract String call
        The SQL query to execute on the database. The result set of the query will be mapped to the datatype specified in the method declaration. This value works in the exact same way as value(), but is used when you wish to specify values other than the SQL query.
        Default:
        ""

      • disconnected

        public abstract boolean disconnected
        Specify whether or not the DataSet resulting from a call to the annotated method will be connected to the database or not.
        See Also:
        DataSet, DataSet.disconnect()
        Default:
        false

      • rubberstamp

        public abstract boolean rubberstamp
        If rubberstamp is flagged as true, the annotated method must return a DataIterator, otherwise it will be rejected by the QueryTool. Rubber-stamping will cause the returned DataIterator to use a single instance of the data-object for all of the rows returned, instead of initializing a new one for each row. This can be used to save CPU time and memory, and is especially useful in display code.
        Default:
        false

      • readOnly

        public abstract boolean readOnly

        By deafult a DataSet returned by an @Call method is read only. If you set this to false the returned DataSet will implement the following additional methods:

        • List.add(Object)
        • List.addAll(java.util.Collection)
        • List.remove(int)
        • List.set(int, Object)

        It is considered a validation error for a method to have readOnly set false if it doesn't return a DataSet.

        Since:
        2.1
        Default:
        true

      • cache

        public abstract Class<? extends DataSetCache> cache

        The cache class to be used by DataSet's returned by the annotated method. This only has an effect of methods that return a DataSet type.

        The default DataSetCache implementation is ArrayDataSetCache, which uses an array to cache the row values. For larger ResultSet's, you may want to look into a NullDataSetCache or using a DataIterator instead of the DataSet class.

        Default:
        net.lemnik.eodsql.ArrayDataSetCache.class

      • resultSetBinding

        public abstract Class<? extends DataObjectBinding> resultSetBinding

        A custom data object binding to be used on the result set of this query. The default value NoDataObjectBinding indicates that no custom binding is to be used.

        Since:
        2.2
        Default:
        net.lemnik.eodsql.spi.util.NoDataObjectBinding.class

      • parameterBindings

        public abstract Class<? extends TypeMapper>[] parameterBindings

        The custom type bindings to be used on the parameters of this query. The binding is matched by position. The default type binding will be used for each parameter that has no parameterBindings entry or an entry that is of type TypeMapper itself.

        Since:
        2.2
        Default:
        {}
